query: What sustainable operating models (local partners, revenue vs subsidy, capacity-building plans) have worked for maintaining digital platforms post-pilot in resource-constrained tourism contexts?

response.query: What sustainable operating models (local partners, revenue vs subsidy, capacity-building plans) have worked for maintaining digital platforms post-pilot in resource-constrained tourism contexts?
response.answer: Sustainable operating models in resource-constrained tourism contexts often rely on subsidies and local partnerships, with a focus on capacity-building for long-term viability. Successful models integrate community involvement and support from international funding agencies. Revenue generation through eco-friendly practices is crucial for sustainability.

results.title: Building strong and resilient tourism destinations
results.content: To achieve a strong and diversified tourism economy, destinations need tailored, forward-looking, and strategic tourism development plans which align with national tourism strategies and address core development needs, such as managing visitor flows, climate change and environmental impacts, digital transition, and crisis management. To maintain social licence and position tourism as a key pillar of regional development, destinations need to manage the trade-offs between economic growth and the impacts on the environment and local communities, so that tourism  9 BUILDING STRONG AND RESILIENT TOURISM DESTINATIONS © OECD 2025 contributes to enhanced living standards and resident well-being.  21 BUILDING STRONG AND RESILIENT TOURISM DESTINATIONS © OECD 2025 The continued growth in visitors and the ongoing management of tourism flows to new destinations will increase the need for tourism data at the local level.

results.content: One of the pillars of action within this ambitious roadmap for a sustainable ocean economy was for sustainable ocean-based tourism, establishing the goal that by 2030 “Coastal and ocean-based tourism is sustainable, resilient, addresses climate change, reduces pollution, supports ecosystem regeneration and biodiversity conservation and invests in local jobs and communities.” To support efforts to deliver on this goal, the Ocean Panel commissioned a body of knowledge on coastal and marine tourism, including this special report.
